clue.text: Deadly obstacle Henry comes up against

parts.note: a let is an obstacle or hindrance, as in 'without let or hindrance'
Hal is the familiar form of Henry, as in Shakespeare's Prince Hal

explanation.surface: A deadly obstruction looms in front of a man called Henry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes up against' just sets the two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lethal is able to kill, which is what deadly means.

clue.text: Way in which churchgoers use most of the legacy, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters may be rearranged into another word
most of says not all the letters are used; one E is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Churchgoers spend most of a bequest on some way into the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops one E from THE LEGACY, and 'possibly' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A lychgate is the roofed gateway into a churchyard, the entrance mourners and worshippers pass through.

clue.text: Money invested in sound annuity

indicators.note: invested in means one piece is put inside another, as money is put into a fund

parts.note: a tone is a sound
tin is slang for money

explanation.surface: Cash is put into a reliable pension scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective (reliable) qualifying the annuity, but it is the noun TONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tontine is an annuity scheme in which subscribers' shares pass to the survivors.

clue.text: Flower needs right time to be cultivated in eastern lands

indicators.note: in places the right-and-time pieces inside the word for eastern lands

parts.note: Asia is the eastern lands, the East

indicators.note: cultivated suggests the soil being worked over, so the letters of time are turned about

explanation.surface: A flower needs the proper season to be grown in Asian countries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be cultivated' signals the anagram of the time letters; 'cultivated' tempts as a gardening word describing the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Artemisia is a genus of flowering plants that includes wormwood and tarragon.

clue.text: Cruel in expression — lets up if distracted

indicators.note: distracted means confused and scattered, so the preceding letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone speaks harshly when their garlands slip because their mind wanders.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram fodder is LETS UP IF, eight letters; the OCR read 'lets' as 'leis'.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiteful remark is a malicious one, cruel in what it says.

clue.text: Some crossing the water have deck games, heading South

parts.note: pontoon is a card game played with a deck
bridge is another card game played with a deck

explanation.surface: Some people crossing water on a ship play cards on deck, heading south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deck games' gives two games, PONTOON and BRIDGE; 'heading South' puts S at the end. 'deck' suggests a ship, but it is a pack of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Pontoon bridges are temporary bridges floated on boats, so they are some of the structures that cross water.

clue.text: Controller of animals from centre of Latin America

indicators.note: centre of picks out the middle letter of the word Latin

parts.note: Amer is an abbreviation for America

explanation.surface: An animal handler comes from Central or Latin America.
explanation.definitionFit: A tamer trains and controls wild animals, as a lion tamer does in a circus.

clue.text: Leaders of task forces run into the enemy

indicators.note: into means the run letter is put inside the word for the enemy

parts.note: foemen is an old word for enemies
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Commanders of military task forces charge into the enemy lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'task forces' suggests the military, but the leaders are workplace supervisors.
explanation.definitionFit: Foremen lead and supervise groups of workers on a job.

clue.text: The French wine having potential

parts.note: la is the French for 'the' (feminine)
tent is a deep red Spanish wine

explanation.surface: French wine shows promise of improving.
explanation.walkthrough: TENT is a red wine from Spain, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Something latent exists but is not yet developed, existing only as potential.

clue.text: Soldier's battlecry if force is in disarray

parts.note: war is battle and a rant is a cry, so the compound word gives two pieces joined

indicators.note: in disarray means the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A soldier yells that the army is in chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battlecry' gives two pieces in one word; 'in disarray' is the anagram signal. The 's stands for 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A warrant officer is a soldier ranking between commissioned and non-commissioned officers.

clue.text: Apply restriction to prisoner taking the air

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner
a strain is a tune or air

explanation.surface: Guards restrict a prisoner going out for some fresh air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'air' suggests the exercise yard, but it is a musical air.
explanation.definitionFit: To constrain is to restrict or hold back.

clue.text: Unlucky French bather married a renegade

parts.note: a rat is a deserter or turncoat

explanation.surface: An ill-fated Frenchwoman in the bath married a traitor.
explanation.walkthrough: Jean-Paul Marat, French revolutionary, was stabbed in his bath by Charlotte Corday.
explanation.definitionFit: The revolutionary Marat was murdered in his bathtub, making him an ill-fated bather.

clue.text: Less pleasant for one who told stories to ruler

parts.note: Grimm, as in the Brothers Grimm, collectors of fairy tales
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Things are less pleasant for a storyteller at the king's court.
explanation.definitionFit: Grimmer is the comparative of grim, meaning more harsh or forbidding.

clue.text: Torment as Roman galley slave, perhaps

indicators.note: torment means twist about painfully, so these letters are wrenched into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Roman torments a slave chained to an oar in a galley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Torment' reads as a verb or noun of suffering, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A galley slave rowed the ship, so is an example of a rower.

clue.text: Hairpiece head removed in anxiety'

indicators.note: head removed means the first letter of the word for anxiety is taken off

parts.note: stress is anxiety

explanation.surface: A wig's top comes off, which causes worry.
explanation.definitionFit: A tress is a long lock of hair, a piece of hair.

clue.text: They-may be knocked over as one over the eight inhibits movement

parts.note: eight plus one is nine; the phrase is also British slang for slightly drunk
pins means holds down, preventing movement

explanation.surface: Things get knocked over when a drunk staggers and loses balance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one over the eight' is British slang for a drink too many, which colours the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninepins are the skittles a bowler knocks over.

clue.text: Commonplace pawn play

parts.note: P is the chess abbreviation for pawn
latitude is freedom of movement, or play

explanation.surface: A pawn move in chess is a routine one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' means slack or room to move, not a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A platitude is a trite remark, a commonplace.

clue.text: One present thanks uplifting nurse

indicators.note: uplifting in a down clue means the word for thanks is read upwards

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks
to tend is to nurse, so a tender is one who nurses

explanation.surface: A guest offers thanks to an encouraging nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: An attender is someone present at an event.

clue.text: Lover's a lascivious type, covered by sheet

indicators.note: covered by means the middle pieces are enclosed by the word for sheet

parts.note: rain that sheets down pours
a ram is a lecherous man

explanation.surface: A lecherous lover is caught under the bedsheet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sheet' looks like bedding but is the verb, as rain sheets down. The 's is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A paramour is an illicit lover.

clue.text: Area producing old port over many years

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the port sits above the years

parts.note: Acre is an ancient port in Israel
an age is a long period of years

explanation.surface: An area produced a historic harbour after many years.
explanation.definitionFit: Acreage is an extent of land measured in acres, an area.

clue.text: Einstein not born to be so perceptive?

indicators.note: not means the letter for born is left out of the scientist's first name

parts.note: Albert Einstein

explanation.surface: Was Einstein so sharp because he wasn't born?
explanation.definitionFit: Alert means watchful and quick to notice, perceptive.

clue.text: According to Cockney, the last runner to back

parts.note: the end is the last part

indicators.note: Cockneys drop their aitches, so the word for runner loses its H

parts.note: a horse is a runner in a race

explanation.surface: A Londoner says the final horse is the one to bet on.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the London East End dialect, known for dropping initial H; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse is to back or support.

clue.text: Surgical procedures held up by-firm plaster

indicators.note: held up in a down clue means the word for surgical procedures reads upwards

parts.note: cuts are what a surgeon makes
Co is short for company, a firm

explanation.surface: Operations were delayed by solid plaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' reads as an adjective with plaster but is a company.
explanation.definitionFit: Stucco is a fine plaster used on walls.

clue.text: Spin employed by cricket side to check continuous running, possibly

parts.note: turn is spin, as of a spun ball
the off side is one half of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A spin bowler is used on the off side to halt a batting run.
explanation.walkthrough: The off side in cricket is the half of the field the batsman faces; cricket terms pervade the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn off a tap or machine stops it running.

clue.text: Beginning performing company

parts.note: on means on stage, performing
a set is a group or company of people

explanation.surface: The start of a touring theatre troupe.
explanation.definitionFit: Onset is the start of something.

clue.text: End wild scrambling for contract

indicators.note: scrambling means mixing up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wild scramble at the end to get a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contract' looks like a noun (a deal) but is the verb, to shrink.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwindle is to shrink, to grow smaller.

clue.text: Stylishness of many a girl

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, hence many
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: Many a girl has elegance.
explanation.definitionFit: Class means elegance or style.

clue.text: One way to settle revolutionary having ups and downs

parts.note: a cheque is one way of paying a bill
a red is a communist revolutionary

explanation.surface: Settling up with a radical has its highs and lows.
explanation.definitionFit: A chequered history is one marked by varied fortunes.

clue.text: Upset open vessel

parts.note: overt means open, not hidden
an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: An open vase is knocked over.
explanation.definitionFit: To overturn is to upset, to knock over.

clue.text: Try again to get male into lift

indicators.note: into means the word for male goes inside the word for lift

parts.note: to rear is to lift up
he is a male pronoun

explanation.surface: Trying again to put a man into the elevator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lift' suggests an elevator but is the verb, to raise.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehear a case in court is to try it again.
